motivation: The preregistered measured-profile experiment's seed-11 binary-only control reached 66.18% on the concentrated 13-model pool. This follow-up tests whether it survives other panels and a shared-supervision refit. That single result and earlier control scores are already known.
method: Freeze the development-selected nominal-large settings, use archived correct/incorrect grades alone on each new candidate's 200 prompts, and the six independent answer channels. Refit both the nominal and the text peer decoder on 75 historical models after excluding every evaluation group. No measured candidate output distributions or candidate test responses go into the fit.
panels: Fifteen independent, common, unique-stem panels with seeds 9200 through 9214 and the same five-source quotas as the original 200-question panel. The deployment example is the first panel. No pooling or best-seed selection.
evaluation: Use the remaining previously unscored canonical groups (419 candidate-corpus questions before missingness filtering), alongside the previous 1,600 and 532 questions and the original 4,985. Report each split separately and the combined withheld bank. Refit all-112 upstream TextMF excluding the entire combined withheld bank, then restrict the competing IDs to the same roster. Compare deterministic and default inference and a panel-selected fixed candidate. Use paired bootstrap intervals over panels and question groups.
additional_full_history_comparison: After observing the refit scores, keep the same 15 panels and use the original 10,748-question encoder unchanged on its original 4,985 and 3,370 held-out prompts. This isolates the effect of changing panels from the effect of retraining the shared encoder on 6,387 questions. The new reserves are excluded from this comparison because the original encoder saw some of those groups.
